answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a bond and commit to a cipher that is a hidden, salted record of claimed independent activity. Random audits test whether supposedly separate agents share control. Proven duplicates lose the bond, while honest agents recover it after the audit window. A Sybil operator must immobilize capital for every fake identity and expects forfeiture on detection, so scaling a swarm raises both funding needs and expected losses. A zenith cap on per-controller influence and a public atlas of audit evidence make the penalty harder to evade.
